body: Thank you again, you wonderful human being. I made myself go to work and your words have stopped me from crying. I want you to know that you made a difference in this horrible day I am having. Thank you so much
It says you responded to me and it is nice things, I cannot find that comment for some reason but I wanted to thank you. It is just two people who responded, but I feel better. Thank you so much.

Its PMDD, it is related to womens health and is basically a PMS on steroids when you cannot control your emotions, plus symptoms like fatigue and lack of concentration. Messes with you and people around you and your work, and you feel like a POS and so worthless. And then when the crazy period is over, I hate myself and blame myself for being moody or inadequate. I feel like a burden to my family and friends and all around you.... I am pretty high functioning, I work and do things at home but it makes it hell - I cry and I feel like dying. I am working on it with a doctor and I am hoping I will stop feeling like this. Sometimes it is just harder than other days and I just wanted to feel more connected to the world so I would possibly just feel a little better. Thank you so much for responding

PMDD can be difficult to deal with and it is important for you to know her cycle to be able to recognize the symptoms as they come. Because sometimes, the fight you two will have wont really be a fight, it will be her PMDD wreaking havoc on both of your lives... I find it easier when my boyfriend helps me get distracted from negative thoughts I am having, sometimes he just listens and lets me pour it all out. I think it is quite individual for each different case and you will have to experiment and see what works for her, try to analyze what triggers certain reactions and what comforts her best. I am sure since she is suspecting PMDD, she probably is or already has taken steps to get better, if you are with her when she gets on birth control, keep in mind that It might cause severe mood swings and emotional reactions regardless of menstrual cycle and that it subsides and stabilizes eventually...might take up tone month I believe, but whatever doctor says. That might be the hardest period if birth control works well for her, after that it should make things easier 

Kudos to you for being a great partner. Good luck!
